correctness.rationale: In cubic generalized Petersen P(n,2), a perfect-matching edge cut is equivalent to a binary 2-coloring with exactly one opposite-color neighbor per vertex. Outer x_i determine d_i<=1 and uniquely force inner y_i=x_i xor(1-d_i); inner equations at offsets ±2 are necessary and sufficient. Every cyclic solution is a closed walk in the 6-bit overlap graph of all admissible 7-bit windows. Fresh independent full 128-window enumeration yielded 28 accepted, iterative zero-in/out pruning removed 20,4,2 states, leaving 12 edges in two loops and two directed five-cycles. This is an exhaustive finite certificate for all n via closed walks, not finite-n extrapolation. Each nontrivial cycle repeats when 5|n, giving 2+10 colorings and hence 1+5 perfect matching cuts after identifying complementary labels in connected P(n,2).
